paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: Ablation studies between Consistency-Bi and Consistency-Uni on test set of IWSLT14 De-En task of wait-k policy.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of three different consistency methods—Consistency-CE, Consistency-Uni, and Consistency-Bi—measured by BLEU score on the IWSLT14 De-En test set under the wait-k policy, as a function of average lagging (AL). The x-axis represents the average lagging, ranging from 1 to 8, with labeled tick marks at 2, 4, 6, and 8. The y-axis represents the BLEU score, scaled linearly from 20 to 32, with major gridlines and labels at intervals of 2. The Consistency-CE method, represented by a purple dotted line with circular markers, shows a steady increase in BLEU score from approximately 19.2 at AL=1 to 31.3 at AL=8. The Consistency-Uni method, shown as a green solid line with square markers, starts at a BLEU score of about 25.2 at AL=1 and rises to 32.1 at AL=8. The Consistency-Bi method, depicted by a red solid line with star markers, begins at a BLEU score of approximately 25.8 at AL=1 and increases to 32.4 at AL=8. Across all values of average lagging, the Consistency-Bi method consistently achieves the highest BLEU score, followed by Consistency-Uni, and then Consistency-CE.
